newsitem.title: USA: Coalition asks tighter rules on captan pesticide.
newsitem.headline: Coalition asks tighter rules on captan pesticide.

text.p: A coalition of U.S. labor unions and environmental groups pressed Wednesday for federal and state action to reduce farmworker exposure to the pesticide captan.

At a news conference, leaders said the group had petitioned the Environmental Protection Agency to require a longer waiting period before workers enter fields treated with captan. They also took the first step toward suing three major strawberry growers for not telling workers that captan was being used.
Richard Trumka, secretary-treasurer of the AFL-CIO, said penalties of several million dollars were possible under terms of California's Proposition 65 warning law.

The coalition asked EPA to re-examine its 1994 decision allowing a 24-hour waiting period to enter strawberry fields instead of a former four-day waiting period. It said EPA made mathematical errors in calculating exposure rates.
"We expect EPA to take another look and set a safe standard," Trumka said at a news conference.
Coalition leaders said captan exposure for field workers was well above the level that under Proposition 65 would require growers to tell workers of the hazard.
"The California law, they are violating right now, sending workers into the field without" a warning, said Brent Blackwelder, president of Friends of the Earth.
So-called "60-day notices" were sent, the coalition said, to Gargiulo Inc, Scurich Brothers, and Garrett Farms, all of Watsonville, California., as well as state and local prosecutors.

Other coalition members were United Farm Workers, Sierra Club, Natural Resources Defense Council, Greenpeace, Headwaters, California Rural Legal Assistance Foundation, Pesticide Action Network, Environmental Working Group, U.S. Public Interest Research Group, Urban Habitat Program, Citizen Clearinghouse for Hazardous Waste, and Farmworkers Justice Fund.
